result: In 39 CFS vs 31 inactive controls on a 45-min 70-degree tilt, CFS had higher heart rate at baseline and on tilt and smaller stroke volume (P<0.05), but positive tilts (11 vs 12) and haemodynamic adjustments did not differ.
reason: Measures stroke volume and HR on tilt by impedance cardiography, no HRV; best fit is the small stroke volume finding, with resting/tilt HR supporting neuro-hrv.

result: In 20 female CFS vs 14 sedentary controls, VO2peak did not differ (28.6 vs 30.9 ml/kg/min), fatigue was higher 24 h after exhaustive treadmill exercise, and immune cell subsets and cytokine mRNA responses did not differ.
reason: Only a single 24-h fatigue rating, no PEM onset or duration data; it does test peak VO2 and finds no significant difference.

result: Blood cytokine mRNA (RT-PCR) and leukocyte subsets measured at baseline, 4 min, 1 h and 24 h after exhaustive exercise did not differ between 20 CFS and 14 sedentary controls.
reason: Post-exercise leukocyte immune mRNA measured and found no group difference, a null result, not an extension; small sample and different gene panel.

result: On 80-degree tilt, 40% of 75 CFS patients had orthostatic intolerance (16 neurally mediated syncope, 7 tachycardia >35 bpm, 6 mixed; about 17% with tachycardia) vs 8/48 controls with syncope only; the OI subgroup was younger with shorter illness and more subacute onset.
reason: Tilt-defined tachycardia in a minority (~17%), within the reported 6-43% range.

result: Heart-rate responses to deep breathing (6/min) and to the Valsalva manoeuvre were similar in 75 CFS patients and 48 controls; 40% of patients had orthostatic intolerance on tilt.
reason: Uses head-up tilt, not the NASA lean test; its normal deep-breathing and Valsalva results bear on the vagal-tone claim instead.

result: PCR found Mycoplasma genus DNA in PBMC of 52% of 100 CFS vs 14% of 50 controls and M. fermentans in 34% vs 8% (P<0.0001), with higher M. fermentans copy numbers (264-2400 vs 130-880 per ug DNA) in patients.
reason: Targeted bacterial (mycoplasma) PCR, not unbiased viral sequencing; no atlas finding covers mycoplasma.

result: In 30 non-depressed CFS vs 15 matched controls, serum morning cortisol was non-significantly lower and evening non-significantly higher, the diurnal cortisol change was significantly smaller (p<0.05), and cortisol measures correlated with functioning.
reason: Same direction for morning cortisol (not significant, small n) and adds a flattened diurnal rhythm and links to disability.

result: Multiplex PCR detected Mycoplasma genus DNA in PBMC of 52% of 100 CFS vs 15% of 100 healthy subjects; M. fermentans 32% vs 8%, M. hominis 9% vs 3%, M. penetrans 6% vs 2%.
reason: Mainly an assay-development paper on bacterial mycoplasma PCR, not viral sequencing; no atlas finding covers mycoplasma.

result: In 150 women with CFS vs 149 clinic controls (self-report questionnaires), cases reported more gynecologic complications, irregular cycles, amenorrhea, intermenstrual bleeding, PCOS, hirsutism and ovarian cysts, and less premenstrual symptomatology.
reason: Same self-reported gynecologic-history approach and direction, but different outcomes (menstrual irregularity, ovarian dysfunction) and a clinic not population sample, so extends rather than replicates.

result: In 21 CFS vs 13 controls, heart rate after tilt (88.9 vs 77.9 bpm, P<0.01) and LF power after tilt (0.603 vs 0.428, P=0.02) were higher, but supine values, deep-breathing and Valsalva responses did not differ and no parasympathetic abnormality was found.
reason: Mixed: tilt HR is higher as in the meta-analysis, but resting measures and vagal tests were normal, against the claimed reduced vagal tone; small sample.
